chapter: Hite tours, postwar L.A. and the Central Avenue scene
title: Eddie Heywood's band: Billy Berg's, Shep's Playhouse, New York
summary: Heywood's band venues, trip to Chicago and Three Deuces, and personnel, then staying home recording until 1951.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: And so you went to work with Eddie Haywood and where did you appear with Eddie Haywood?
Well, we were with Billie Berg's (PHONETIC) out on Vine. Then we went down to Shep's Playhouse.
Shep's Playhouse was where?
That was in Chinatown and old Japanese-town.
Bronzeville ?
That was what they called (inaudible)?
I don't know, but it was in part of the town that the --
Japanese (inaudible)
-- that the Japanese were evicted from during World War II.
Down on First Street.

That's right. Down First, Second, Third Street, around that area there. It was a place called Shep's Playhouse. So we worked there over the Christmas vacations that particular year, which was 1945, and we left and took a train into Chicago and played a couple of dates around that area. and then took a train on into New York and went to work to Three Deuces on 52nd Street, which was very interesting, because we were working for Three Deuces and next door, Art Tatum was working at a joint and next door to him, Dizzy Gillespie was working in a joint, and so on, right on down the street. So, it
was very good. I stayed with Eddie Haywood until April of 1946.
Who else was with Eddie Haywood in the band when you were with him? (inaudible)?

Well, the trombones were Vic Dickenson and Henry Coker. Par Jones was the trumpet player. Ernie Shepherd was the bass player and I'm still trying to think of what that little drummer player's name was out of Brooklyn. Keg Parnell (PHONETIC). And Eddie, of course, was the pianist. So, I worked with them until April. Then I came back home. I didn't hardly budge out of Los Angeles until I went with the Basie Band.
That was like 5 years, right?
(inaudible).
That's right, stayed right here. I wouldn't even go hardly to San Diego to play. I just stayed right here and didn't do anything but record and just stay around town, mostly recordings.
That was when you made the record with Frank Sinatra and probably a lot of... (inaudible).
Yes.
Who all else did you record with?
I don't know, just whoever called, you know?
